message:
test(host): find out where PrintWindow actually sends the request

Test 1, build 1. No product change.

This was meant to be the negative control for the preview deadline: a window that pumps
messages and never returns from WM_PRINT, and a check that today's capture cannot answer in
time against it. The fixture works and is the right shape -- it keeps dispatching, so WM_NULL
comes back and IsHungAppWindow calls it healthy, which is the guard host_bgra_scale.cpp relies
on and the reason that guard was never going to be enough.

The check failed, and the reason is the finding. capture_window_thumbnail asks for
PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT, and on this OS that is served out of the DWM redirection surface: the
capture returns a correct 256x154 thumbnail in ~24ms from a window that would never have
answered, and the window's own WM_PRINT counter is still zero afterwards. Not inferred -- the
fixture counts what it receives and the parent asks it.

So the suite asserts what is true instead. If a future Windows starts dispatching WM_PRINT for
these flags, the zero-count check fails and says so, and a WM_PRINT fixture becomes usable
again. The deadline's negative control moves to the helper boundary, where a stall can be
injected into a process we own, and that is part of the step still waiting on a decision.

Two consequences worth stating plainly.

It narrows the incident. If the request never reaches the application then "LDPlayer did not
answer WM_PRINT" cannot be what held the control session for 1h50m on 2026-09-15. That was
already recorded as an inference rather than a finding, and it is now a weak one: the block has
to be on the DWM/GPU side, which is also where that morning's TDR was -- amdkmdag.sys, named in
the kernel mini-dump two commits ago.

And it settles a design question that was still open. A block inside DWM cannot be cancelled
from user mode, so an in-process worker thread could never be reclaimed -- no timeout, no
cancellation, nothing short of ending the process. Isolation is not the tidier of two options
here; it is the only one that can recover.

The baseline the deadline will be set from, measured over 12 captures per size, stable across
four runs: 640x480 and 1280x800 both ~16ms median, 1920x1080 ~33ms median and 35ms worst. That
matches the ~33ms the picker's own comment already claimed. A one second deadline is roughly
thirty times the worst case seen here.

What these numbers are not: real application windows. Every one of them is this file's own
fixture, and the task forbids pointing the probe at the user's applications. A window backed by
a large GPU surface could cost more.

The harness cannot hang. The probe runs in a child process, the parent waits with a limit, and
a job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE takes every child when it closes -- including one still
inside WM_PRINT, which the last check confirms.
